subject: math
title: Mean, Median, Mode and Range
seo_title: Grade 6 Mean, Median, Mode and Range Worksheets: Dot Plots, Outliers and IQR with Answer Key
standard_text: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 mean, median, mode and range worksheets: find the median of even and odd data sets, compute the mean, read dot plots, see how outliers change the mean, find the IQR and a missing score. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Mean = sum ÷ count. Median = middle value after sorting. Range = greatest − least.
key_sub: The mode is the value that appears most often. With an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values. An outlier pulls the mean, but not the median.
body_html:
Center and variation

A measure of center sums up a whole data set with one number: the mean or the median. The mode also tells which value is most typical. A measure of variation tells, with one number, how spread out the values are: the range or the interquartile range (IQR).

Seven quiz scores: 8, 5, 9, 6, 9, 3, 9. Sorted: 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9.

MeasureHow to find itExample
MeanAdd all the values. Divide by how many values there are.49 ÷ 7 = 7
MedianSort the values. Take the middle one.3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9 → 8
ModeThe value that appears most often9 appears 3 times → 9
RangeGreatest − least9 − 3 = 6

Median of an even number of values

With an even count there are two middle values. The median is their mean, so it can end in .5.

Example

Find the median of 12, 7, 10, 15, 9, 14.

Sort: 7, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15. There are 6 values, so the middle values are the 3rd and 4th: 10 and 12. (10 + 12) ÷ 2 = 11.

Answer: 11

Read a dot plot

Each X is one value. Ten students told how many books they read last month.

Mean: 0 × 1 + 1 × 3 + 2 × 2 + 3 × 2 + 4 × 1 + 8 × 1 = 25, and 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5. Median: the 5th and 6th X's from the left are both at 2, so the median is 2. Mode: the tallest stack is at 1. Range: 8 − 0 = 8.

Outliers: mean or median?

An outlier is a value far from the others, like the 8 above. It pulls the mean toward it, but it barely moves the median. Here the mean (2.5) is greater than the median (2). When a data set has an outlier, the median usually describes a typical value better.

Interquartile range (IQR)

Sort the data and find the median. Q1 is the median of the lower half and Q3 is the median of the upper half. When the count is odd, leave the middle value out of both halves. IQR = Q3 − Q1.

Example

Find the IQR of the quiz scores 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9.

The median is 8. Lower half: 3, 5, 6, so Q1 = 5. Upper half: 9, 9, 9, so Q3 = 9. IQR = 9 − 5 = 4.

Answer: 4

Find a missing value

Example

Ava’s first 4 test scores are 82, 88, 79 and 87. What score does she need on the 5th test to have a mean of 85?

For a mean of 85 on 5 tests, the total must be 5 × 85 = 425. So far: 82 + 88 + 79 + 87 = 336. 425 − 336 = 89.

Answer: 89

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking the middle of the list without sortingSort from least to greatest first
Picking one middle value when the count is evenUse the mean of the two middle values
Dividing by the wrong count for the meanDivide by how many values there are (count the X's on a dot plot)
Giving the greatest value as the rangeRange = greatest − least
Giving the count as the mode (“3 times”)The mode is the value that repeats, not how many times
Mixing up mean and medianMean: add and divide. Median: sort and take the middle
Averaging two group means of different sizesFind each total, add them, then divide by everyone

faq.q: How do you find the mean, median, mode and range?
faq.a: Mean: add the values and divide by how many there are. Median: sort the values and take the middle one. Mode: the value that appears most often. Range: greatest value minus least value.

faq.q: How do you find the median when there is an even number of values?
faq.a: Sort the values and find the two middle ones, then take their mean. For 7, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15 the middle values are 10 and 12, so the median is 11.

faq.q: What is the difference between a measure of center and a measure of variation?
faq.a: A measure of center (mean or median) gives one typical value for the data. A measure of variation (range or interquartile range) gives one number for how spread out the values are.

faq.q: When is the median better than the mean?
faq.a: When the data has an outlier or is very lopsided. One very large or very small value pulls the mean toward it, but the median stays near the middle of the data.

items.q: Hana saved money for 9 weeks. The amounts she saved, in dollars, are 24, 15, 9, 20, 22, 5, 20, 12, 4. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 4, 5, 9, 12, 15, 20, 20, 22, 24. With 9 values, the middle one is the 5th: 15. (The middle of the unsorted list, 22, is not the median.)

items.q: Jack's scores on 7 spelling tests (out of 20) are 19, 20, 17, 17, 16, 16, 16. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 16 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 16, not the count 3.

items.q: Theo counted the birds at a feeder on 9 mornings. The counts are 18, 6, 6, 5, 22, 16, 20, 9, 6. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 22 − 5 = 17. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: The numbers of students on 6 school buses are 50, 32, 44, 43, 29, 30. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 29, 30, 32, 43, 44, 50. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 32 and 43. The median is their mean: (32 + 43) ÷ 2 = 37.5.

items.q: The times, in seconds, of 7 runners in a 100-meter race are 22, 19, 18, 14, 17, 14, 13. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 13, 14, 14, 17, 18, 19, 22. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 17. (The middle of the unsorted list, 14, is not the median.)

items.q: Nora read every day for 7 days. The numbers of pages she read are 35, 19, 40, 40, 31, 40, 19. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 40 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 40, not the count 3.

items.q: At swim practice, 9 swimmers counted their laps. The numbers of laps are 14, 13, 9, 27, 14, 14, 29, 22, 15. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 29 − 9 = 20. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: The ages of 10 cousins, in years, are 8, 6, 5, 7, 17, 10, 14, 16, 7, 12. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 17. With 10 values, there are two middle values, the 5th and 6th: 8 and 10. The median is their mean: (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9.

items.q: Mia scored these points in 5 basketball games: 8, 12, 25, 25, 11. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 8, 11, 12, 25, 25. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 12. (The middle of the unsorted list, 25, is not the median.)

items.q: The prices of 8 books at a used-book sale, in dollars, are 4, 9, 5, 4, 14, 14, 8, 14. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 14 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 14, not the count 3.

items.q: The heights of 9 tomato plants, in inches, are 14, 18, 15, 20, 30, 12, 24, 14, 27. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 30 − 12 = 18. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: The numbers of cars in a parking lot at 8 different times were 28, 55, 29, 59, 59, 20, 49, 46. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 20, 28, 29, 46, 49, 55, 59, 59. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 46 and 49. The median is their mean: (46 + 49) ÷ 2 = 47.5.

items.q: Sam did push-ups every day for 8 days. The numbers of push-ups he did are 15, 19, 11, 11, 24, 35, 19, 14. What is the mode?
items.e: 11 and 19 each appear 2 times. Every other value appears once. A data set can have two modes: 11 and 19.

items.q: The weights of 7 puppies at a shelter, in pounds, are 5, 7, 20, 21, 5, 16, 22. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 5, 5, 7, 16, 20, 21, 22. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 16. (The middle of the unsorted list, 21, is not the median.)

items.q: A teacher asked 10 students to time their walk to school. The times, in minutes, are 12, 9, 24, 15, 5, 15, 18, 18, 17, 18. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 18 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 18, not the count 3.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, for 6 days in May were 73, 69, 73, 82, 75, 81. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 82 − 69 = 13. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: Luis saved money for 6 weeks. The amounts he saved, in dollars, are 14, 8, 4, 19, 21, 16. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 4, 8, 14, 16, 19, 21. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 14 and 16. The median is their mean: (14 + 16) ÷ 2 = 15.

items.q: Chloe's scores on 6 spelling tests (out of 20) are 16, 13, 19, 17, 14, 15. What is the mode?
items.e: Each value appears only once, so no value is more common than the others. The data set has no mode. (The mode is never a count like 1.)

items.q: Emma counted the birds at a feeder on 9 mornings. The counts are 6, 16, 6, 20, 15, 14, 9, 17, 17. What is the mode?
items.e: 6 and 17 each appear 2 times. Every other value appears once. A data set can have two modes: 6 and 17.

items.q: The numbers of students on 10 school buses are 40, 31, 52, 29, 39, 47, 43, 39, 51, 49. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 29, 31, 39, 39, 40, 43, 47, 49, 51, 52. With 10 values, there are two middle values, the 5th and 6th: 40 and 43. The median is their mean: (40 + 43) ÷ 2 = 41.5.

items.q: Ben scored these points in 6 basketball games: 16, 23, 23, 20, 25, 25. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 16 + 23 + 23 + 20 + 25 + 25 = 132. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 132 ÷ 6 = 22.

items.q: The numbers of students on 6 school buses are 30, 34, 37, 37, 38, 28. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 30 + 34 + 37 + 37 + 38 + 28 = 204. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 204 ÷ 6 = 34.

items.q: The weights of 5 puppies at a shelter, in pounds, are 5, 19, 13, 10, 13. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 5 + 19 + 13 + 10 + 13 = 60. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 60 ÷ 5 = 12.

items.q: Maya did push-ups every day for 5 days. The numbers of push-ups she did are 39, 13, 30, 24, 39. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 39 + 13 + 30 + 24 + 39 = 145. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 145 ÷ 5 = 29.

items.q: The times, in seconds, of 5 runners in a 100-meter race are 18, 20, 17, 20, 20. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 18 + 20 + 17 + 20 + 20 = 95. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 95 ÷ 5 = 19.

items.q: At swim practice, 6 swimmers counted their laps. The numbers of laps are 27, 22, 28, 22, 17, 19. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 27 + 22 + 28 + 22 + 17 + 19 = 135. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 135 ÷ 6 = 22.5.

items.q: The heights of 7 tomato plants, in inches, are 30, 18, 16, 25, 17, 31, 31. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 30 + 18 + 16 + 25 + 17 + 31 + 31 = 168. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 168 ÷ 7 = 24.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, for 5 days in May were 74, 72, 72, 61, 71. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 74 + 72 + 72 + 61 + 71 = 350. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 350 ÷ 5 = 70.

items.q: Leo read every day for 6 days. The numbers of pages he read are 15, 45, 17, 41, 25, 25. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 15 + 45 + 17 + 41 + 25 + 25 = 168. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 168 ÷ 6 = 28.

items.q: The mean of 5 test scores is 81. What is the sum of the 5 scores?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count. Sum = 81 × 5 = 405 points.

items.q: Ruby counted the birds at a feeder on 6 mornings. The counts are 7, 5, 12, 18, 17, 13. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 7 + 5 + 12 + 18 + 17 + 13 = 72. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 72 ÷ 6 = 12.

items.q: The numbers of cars in a parking lot at 6 different times were 50, 41, 21, 36, 20, 60. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 50 + 41 + 21 + 36 + 20 + 60 = 228. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 228 ÷ 6 = 38.

items.q: A teacher asked 8 students to time their walk to school. The times, in minutes, are 23, 25, 15, 13, 6, 16, 21, 21. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 23 + 25 + 15 + 13 + 6 + 16 + 21 + 21 = 140. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 140 ÷ 8 = 17.5.

items.q: Ava read for 7 days. She read a mean of 24 pages per day. How many pages did she read in all?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count. Sum = 24 × 7 = 168 pages.

items.q: The ages of 5 cousins, in years, are 8, 13, 4, 6, 14. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 8 + 13 + 4 + 6 + 14 = 45. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 45 ÷ 5 = 9.

items.q: Sofia's scores on 5 spelling tests (out of 20) are 16, 14, 19, 13, 13. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 16 + 14 + 19 + 13 + 13 = 75. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 75 ÷ 5 = 15.

items.q: The prices of 8 books at a used-book sale, in dollars, are 6, 15, 7, 10, 9, 15, 15, 15. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 6 + 15 + 7 + 10 + 9 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 92. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 92 ÷ 8 = 11.5.

items.q: The mean weight of 7 backpacks is 14 pounds. What is the total weight of the backpacks?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count. Sum = 14 × 7 = 98 pounds.

items.q: Zoe saved money for 5 weeks. The amounts she saved, in dollars, are 21, 4, 15, 7, 13. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 21 + 4 + 15 + 7 + 13 = 60. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 60 ÷ 5 = 12.

items.q: Lily scored these points in 6 basketball games: 23, 16, 26, 26, 11, 21. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 23 + 16 + 26 + 26 + 11 + 21 = 123. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 123 ÷ 6 = 20.5.

items.q: In a survey, 10 students counted the pets they have at home. How many students are shown on the dot plot?
items.e: Each X is one student. Add the X's in every column: 1 + 4 + 4 + 1 = 10.

items.q: A class survey asked 11 students how many books they read last month. What is the mode of the data?
items.e: The tallest stack of X's is above 2, so the mode is 2. (The stack has 5 X's, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: The dot plot shows how many hours each of 13 band members practiced last week. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 2 and the X farthest to the right is at 6. Range = 6 − 2 = 4. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many runs a softball team scored in each of 12 games. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 12 X's. The two middle X's are the 6th and 7th from the left. Both are above 6, so the median is 6.

items.q: The dot plot shows the goals Ben's soccer team scored in 12 games. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 0 × 1 + 1 × 3 + 2 × 3 + 3 × 1 + 4 × 2 + 5 × 2 = 30. There are 12 X's, so divide by 12: 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5.

items.q: In a class, 9 students counted the letters in their first names. What is the mode of the data?
items.e: The tallest stack of X's is above 7, so the mode is 7. (The stack has 3 X's, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: In a survey, 14 students recorded how many hours they slept last night. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 14 X's. The two middle X's are the 7th and 8th from the left. Both are above 9, so the median is 9.

items.q: In a class, 12 students took a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows their scores. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 4 and the X farthest to the right is at 10. Range = 10 − 4 = 6. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: In a survey, 11 students counted the pets they have at home. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 0 × 1 + 1 × 1 + 2 × 2 + 3 × 1 + 4 × 5 + 5 × 1 = 33. There are 11 X's, so divide by 11: 33 ÷ 11 = 3.

items.q: A class survey asked 9 students how many books they read last month. How many students are shown on the dot plot?
items.e: Each X is one student. Add the X's in every column: 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 9.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many hours each of 11 band members practiced last week. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 11 X's. The median is the 6th X when you count from the left. It is above 7, so the median is 7.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many runs a softball team scored in each of 12 games. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 1 × 2 + 3 × 4 + 4 × 2 + 5 × 1 + 6 × 1 + 7 × 1 + 8 × 1 = 48. There are 12 X's, so divide by 12: 48 ÷ 12 = 4.

items.q: The dot plot shows the goals Leo's soccer team scored in 14 games. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 1 and the X farthest to the right is at 5. Range = 5 − 1 = 4. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: In a class, 11 students counted the letters in their first names. What is the mode of the data?
items.e: The tallest stack of X's is above 7, so the mode is 7. (The stack has 5 X's, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: In a survey, 10 students recorded how many hours they slept last night. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 10 X's. The two middle X's are the 5th and 6th from the left. Both are above 7, so the median is 7.

items.q: In a class, 9 students took a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows their scores. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 5 × 1 + 7 × 3 + 9 × 4 + 10 × 1 = 72. There are 9 X's, so divide by 9: 72 ÷ 9 = 8.

items.q: In a survey, 10 students counted the pets they have at home. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 0 and the X farthest to the right is at 4. Range = 4 − 0 = 4. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: A class survey asked 9 students how many books they read last month. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 9 X's. The median is the 5th X when you count from the left. It is above 5, so the median is 5.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many hours each of 9 band members practiced last week. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 2 × 1 + 5 × 1 + 6 × 2 + 7 × 5 = 54. There are 9 X's, so divide by 9: 54 ÷ 9 = 6.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many runs a softball team scored in each of 9 games. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 1 × 3 + 2 × 2 + 4 × 2 + 6 × 2 = 27. There are 9 X's, so divide by 9: 27 ÷ 9 = 3.

items.q: The prices, in dollars, of 7 T-shirts in a store are 12, 19, 60, 15, 18, 19, 20. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 12 and 20. The value 60 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: The weights, in pounds, of 6 dogs at a dog park are 103, 21, 34, 30, 22, 33. The outlier, 103, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 103 there are 5 values. Their sum is 21 + 34 + 30 + 22 + 33 = 140. Mean = 140 ÷ 5 = 28. (With the outlier the mean was 243 ÷ 6 = 40.5.)

items.q: The ages of 7 people at a family picnic are 34, 34, 37, 36, 40, 40, 3. Which measure best describes a typical value?
items.e: The outlier 3 pulls the mean down to 32, which is less than every other value. The median, 36, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: A teacher asked 4 students to time their walk to school. The times, in minutes, are 21, 4, 11, 24. The mean is 15. The value 25 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 60 + 25 = 85, and now there are 5 values. New mean = 85 ÷ 5 = 17. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

items.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 18. Five of them are 20, 17, 11, 18, 11. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 6 numbers must be 6 × 18 = 108. The known numbers add to 20 + 17 + 11 + 18 + 11 = 77. Missing number = 108 − 77 = 31.

items.q: Luis's scores on 8 spelling tests (out of 20) are 12, 19, 17, 11, 19, 18, 16, 20. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
The heights, in inches, of 7 sunflowers are 66, 64, 67, 63, 59, 69, 67. Which number describes how much the values vary?
items.e: The mean, median and mode are measures of center: each gives one typical value. The range is a measure of variation: 69 − 59 = 10 tells how spread out the values are. So the answer is the range, 10.

items.q: Emma recorded how long, in minutes, she spent on homework on 7 nights: 27, 42, 5, 44, 35, 33, 38. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 27 and 44. The value 5 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: Omar counted the emails he got on 7 days: 64, 10, 13, 13, 20, 17, 17. The outlier, 64, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 64 there are 6 values. Their sum is 10 + 13 + 13 + 20 + 17 + 17 = 90. Mean = 90 ÷ 6 = 15. (With the outlier the mean was 154 ÷ 7 = 22.)

items.q: The numbers of pages in 8 books on a shelf are 204, 252, 208, 228, 192, 236, 249, 687. Which measure best describes a typical value?
items.e: The outlier 687 pulls the mean up to 282, which is greater than every other value. The median, 232, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: Eli scored these points in 5 basketball games: 15, 9, 9, 23, 24. The mean is 16. The value 10 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 80 + 10 = 90, and now there are 6 values. New mean = 90 ÷ 6 = 15. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 18. Four of them are 23, 13, 22, 17. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 5 numbers must be 5 × 18 = 90. The known numbers add to 23 + 13 + 22 + 17 = 75. Missing number = 90 − 75 = 15.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, for 9 days in May were 80, 71, 71, 63, 68, 83, 76, 66, 64. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Sort first: 63, 64, 66, 68, 71, 71, 76, 80, 83. The median is 71. Leave it out of both halves. Lower half: 63, 64, 66, 68, so Q1 = 65. Upper half: 71, 76, 80, 83, so Q3 = 78. IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 78 − 65 = 13.

items.q: The numbers of visitors to a small museum on 8 days were 67, 42, 55, 186, 51, 43, 52, 48. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 42 and 67. The value 186 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: Hana rode her bike to school on 7 days. The times, in minutes, were 18, 18, 12, 13, 17, 12, 43. The outlier, 43, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 43 there are 6 values. Their sum is 18 + 18 + 12 + 13 + 17 + 12 = 90. Mean = 90 ÷ 6 = 15. (With the outlier the mean was 133 ÷ 7 = 19.)

items.q: The prices, in dollars, of 8 T-shirts in a store are 18, 14, 16, 20, 18, 54, 12, 16. Which measure best describes a typical value?
items.e: The outlier 54 pulls the mean up to 21, which is greater than every other value. The median, 17, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: The numbers of cars in a parking lot at 4 different times were 24, 54, 25, 29. The mean is 33. The value 53 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 132 + 53 = 185, and now there are 5 values. New mean = 185 ÷ 5 = 37. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

items.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 22. Five of them are 27, 23, 21, 18, 23. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 6 numbers must be 6 × 22 = 132. The known numbers add to 27 + 23 + 21 + 18 + 23 = 112. Missing number = 132 − 112 = 20.

items.q: The weights, in pounds, of 7 dogs at a dog park are 21, 22, 18, 18, 31, 28, 23. Which number describes how much the values vary?
items.e: The mean, median and mode are measures of center: each gives one typical value. The range is a measure of variation: 31 − 18 = 13 tells how spread out the values are. So the answer is the range, 13.

items.q: Leo saved money for 7 weeks. The amounts he saved, in dollars, are 15, 10, 15, 12, 18, 7, 19. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Sort first: 7, 10, 12, 15, 15, 18, 19. The median is 15. Leave it out of both halves. Lower half: 7, 10, 12, so Q1 = 10. Upper half: 15, 18, 19, so Q3 = 18. IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 18 − 10 = 8.

items.q: Chloe read for 60, 45, 60, 40, 30, 50, 25, 45, 20, 15 minutes on 10 days. What is the median number of minutes she read?
items.e: Sort first: 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 45, 45, 50, 60, 60. With 10 values, there are two middle values, the 5th and 6th: 40 and 45. The median is their mean: (40 + 45) ÷ 2 = 42.5.

items.q: Kai's scores in 4 bowling games are 107, 112, 102, 137. What score does he need in the next game to average 120 for all 5 games?
items.e: To have a mean of 120 over 5 bowling games, the total must be 5 × 120 = 600. So far: 107 + 112 + 102 + 137 = 458. Kai needs 600 − 458 = 142.

items.q: Nora's scores on the first 4 tests are 73, 96, 80, 77. What score does she need on the 5th test to have a mean score of 85?
items.e: To have a mean of 85 over 5 tests, the total must be 5 × 85 = 425. So far: 73 + 96 + 80 + 77 = 326. Nora needs 425 − 326 = 99.

items.q: Mia scored 18, 26, 18, 12, 19 points in 5 basketball games. How many points does she need in the next game to average 18 points per game?
items.e: To have a mean of 18 over 6 basketball games, the total must be 6 × 18 = 108. So far: 18 + 26 + 18 + 12 + 19 = 93. Mia needs 108 − 93 = 15.

items.q: A bakery sold 43, 39, 51, 36, 47, 39 muffins on 6 days. What is the range of the number of muffins sold?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 51 − 36 = 15.

items.q: Noah averaged 15 points per game in 4 games. Then he scored 25 points in the next game. What is his new average for all 5 games?
items.e: Points before: 15 × 4 = 60. New total: 60 + 25 = 85. New average = 85 ÷ 5 = 17 points.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, in Denver from Monday to Sunday were 48, 59, 61, 63, 54, 54, 60. What was the mean high temperature?
items.e: Add the values: 48 + 59 + 61 + 63 + 54 + 54 + 60 = 399. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 399 ÷ 7 = 57. The mean high temperature was 57°F.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, in Seattle from Monday to Sunday were 58, 65, 63, 58, 65, 64, 52. What was the range of the temperatures?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 65 − 52 = 13.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class grew 8 bean plants. After 3 weeks, the heights in centimeters were 20, 10, 13, 9, 16, 10, 15, 12. What was the median height?
items.e: Sort first: 9, 10, 10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 20. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 12 and 13. The median is their mean: (12 + 13) ÷ 2 = 12.5.

items.q: In a class, 7 girls read a mean of 10 books over the summer and 3 boys read a mean of 5 books. What is the mean number of books for all 10 students?
items.e: Find each total first: 7 × 10 = 70 and 3 × 5 = 15. All together: 70 + 15 = 85 books for 10 students. Mean = 85 ÷ 10 = 8.5. (Averaging 10 and 5 does not work, because the groups are different sizes.)

items.q: On 5 quizzes, Sam scored 6, 9, 10, 10, 10 and Owen scored 6, 8, 10, 10, 6. How many points greater is Sam's mean score than Owen's?
Ruby's scores on the first 3 tests are 81, 91, 92. What score does she need on the 4th test to have a mean score of 90?
items.e: To have a mean of 90 over 4 tests, the total must be 4 × 90 = 360. So far: 81 + 91 + 92 = 264. Ruby needs 360 − 264 = 96.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class grew 8 bean plants. After 3 weeks, the heights in centimeters were 20, 13, 12, 13, 22, 19, 18, 11. What is the difference between the mean and the median?
items.e: Mean: 20 + 13 + 12 + 13 + 22 + 19 + 18 + 11 = 128, and 128 ÷ 8 = 16. Median: Sort first: 11, 12, 13, 13, 18, 19, 20, 22. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 13 and 18. The median is their mean: (13 + 18) ÷ 2 = 15.5. Difference: 16 − 15.5 = 0.5.

items.q: In 5 long jumps, Zoe jumped 14, 9, 14, 14, 14 feet and Lily jumped 13, 9, 11, 8, 9 feet. How many feet greater is Zoe's mean jump than Lily's?
Ava averaged 19 points per game in 6 games. How many points did she score in all?
items.e: Total = mean × number of games = 19 × 6 = 114 points.

items.q: A basketball team scored 59, 43, 40, 39, 53, 50, 40, 56 points in its first 8 games. What was the mean number of points per game?
items.e: Add the values: 59 + 43 + 40 + 39 + 53 + 50 + 40 + 56 = 380. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 380 ÷ 8 = 47.5.

items.q: Luis saved 19, 16, 18, 6, 10, 15 dollars in 6 weeks. What is the mean amount he saved per week, in dollars?
items.e: Add the values: 19 + 16 + 18 + 6 + 10 + 15 = 84. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 84 ÷ 6 = 14.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class grew 8 bean plants. After 3 weeks, the heights in centimeters were 10, 14, 17, 19, 15, 19, 9, 17. What was the mean height?
items.e: Add the values: 10 + 14 + 17 + 19 + 15 + 19 + 9 + 17 = 120. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 120 ÷ 8 = 15. The mean height was 15 cm.

items.q: On the red team, 6 players scored a mean of 9 points. On the blue team, 5 players scored a mean of 20 points. What is the mean score of all 11 players?
items.e: Find each total first: 6 × 9 = 54 and 5 × 20 = 100. All together: 54 + 100 = 154 points for 11 players. Mean = 154 ÷ 11 = 14. (Averaging 9 and 20 does not work, because the groups are different sizes.)

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, in Phoenix from Monday to Sunday were 87, 94, 97, 98, 90, 95, 85. What was the median high temperature?
items.e: Sort first: 85, 87, 90, 94, 95, 97, 98. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 94.
